title: Leaker Unveils Bigger iPhone Duo Specs, Including Potential Telephoto Camera Upgrade
body:
Apple’s next-generation iPhone Duo is poised to break new ground, according to a prolific leaker who shared fresh details on Mark Gurman’s Power On podcast. The insider suggests that Apple will introduce significantly larger display options for the dual‑screen device, potentially expanding the screen size to 7.5 inches or more. In addition, rumours point to the inclusion of a dedicated telephoto lens, a feature that could finally bring true optical zoom to the foldable form factor. These revelations hint at a more ambitious hardware roadmap for Apple’s folding‑phone ambitions, signaling that the company may be ready to challenge both its own iPhone lineup and rival Android foldables in the coming years.

The leaker, known for accurate Apple predictions, described the upcoming iPhone Duo as “the biggest screen Apple has ever put in a hand‑held.” While Apple’s current iPhone Pro Max models top out at 6.7 inches, the new Duo could push the envelope to a 7.5‑inch main display when unfolded, with a secondary screen of roughly 4.5 inches on the outside. This size increase would not only make multitasking more practical but also align the Duo with premium Android foldables such as the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 5 and the Huawei Mate X series, which already boast expansive displays. Analysts believe the larger panel could help Apple overcome one of the major criticisms of its earlier foldable prototypes: a cramped user experience that limited productivity and media consumption.

Beyond the screen, the leaker hinted at a major camera upgrade: a dedicated telephoto lens on the Duo’s rear module. Historically, Apple’s foldable concepts have relied on a single wide‑angle sensor, limiting the device’s photographic versatility compared to the iPhone’s multi‑camera arrays. Introducing a telephoto unit would bring optical zoom—likely 2× or 3×—to the foldable, closing a gap that has persisted since the first iPhone’s camera evolution. Industry insiders suggest that the telephoto sensor could be housed within a thin, flexible module that folds with the rest of the device, a technical challenge Apple has reportedly been refining for the past two years.

These speculations arrive at a pivotal moment for Apple’s hardware strategy. The company has been cautious with foldables, releasing only limited‑edition prototypes and keeping production timelines vague. Yet the market for foldable smartphones has grown steadily, with global shipments projected to exceed 30 million units this year, driven by consumer appetite for larger screens without sacrificing portability. Apple’s entry into this segment could reshape the competitive landscape, especially if the Duo delivers a seamless integration of iOS, robust app support, and the premium build quality the brand is known for. Moreover, a larger, telephoto‑equipped Duo would reinforce Apple’s narrative that foldables are not just gimmicks but genuine productivity tools for power users.

Critics, however, caution that Apple’s first commercial foldable will need to address durability concerns that have plagued earlier models from other manufacturers. The hinge mechanism, flexible display longevity, and repairability remain key variables that could influence consumer adoption. Apple’s track record of perfecting hardware through iterative refinements—evident in the evolution of the iPhone and Apple Watch—suggests the company may be willing to wait for the right moment rather than rush a premature launch. If the Duo does arrive with the rumored larger screen and telephoto lens, it will likely debut in the latter half of 2025, aligning with Apple’s typical September‑October product cadence.

Looking ahead, the iPhone Duo could set a new benchmark for what a premium smartphone can achieve, blending the expansive canvas of a tablet with the pocketability of a phone. Should Apple deliver on the leaker’s claims, the device may usher in a new era of iOS‑centric foldables, prompting developers to craft apps that fully exploit the dual‑screen experience. As the industry watches closely, the next few months will reveal whether Apple’s ambitious roadmap will materialise into a market‑defining product, or remain another tantalising whisper in the ever‑evolving saga of foldable technology.
